articles.title: 'Peeping Tom gets out': Man who allegedly hid three spy cameras in Hong Kong gym changing rooms out on bail
articles.description: A Hong Kong man who allegedly installed pinhole cameras in changing rooms at a branch of a popular gym chain has been released on bail pending further police investigation to identify potential victims. Construction site foreman Fung Kwok-wang, 34, was not required to answer a count of voyeurism during his first appearance at Sha Tin Court on Tuesday, as prosecutors sought an eight-week adjournment for further police inquiries. Acting Principal Magistrate Cheang Kei-hong granted the defendant HK$2,000 (US$255) bail on condition that he remain in Hong Kong, avoid contact with prosecution witnesses and stay away from the 24/7 Fitness branch on Lek Yuen Street in Sha Tin. The case will be heard again on November 25. The fitness centre reported the case to police on Friday after a customer spotted a small camera secured with black tape in the false ceiling of a changing room. Police combed through the premises and seized three pinhole cameras and three 12GB memory cards from three of the four individual unisex changing rooms. Officers subsequently recovered multiple video clips filmed between September 23 and 25. Fung was arrested shortly after 9pm on Sunday. The Sha Tin district investigation team is handling the case. Voyeurism is punishable by up to five years in prison, which is capped at two years when the case is heard by a magistrate.

articles.title: Hong Kong man charged with voyeurism over hiding pinhole cameras in gym
articles.description: A Hong Kong man has been charged with voyeurism after he was arrested for allegedly installing hidden pinhole cameras in a gym changing room. Fung Kwok-wang, a 34-year-old worksite foreman, left the Shatin Magistrates' Courts on Tuesday morning after being granted bail. He was arrested on Sunday, after videos of a pinhole camera taped to a removable ceiling panel circulated on social media. The camera was discovered by a staff member at a 24/7 Fitness branch in Sha Tin, police said. According to a court document, Fung was charged with one count of voyeurism, alleging that he installed or operated a pinhole camera at the Sha Tin gym between September 24 and 25 to enable himself or any other person to commit a voyeurism offence under the city's Crimes Ordinance. The gym chain has suspended Fung's membership and stepped up checks across all branches. Storage devices seized Police said in a Monday press conference that three pinhole cameras were found in the changing rooms at the gym on Lek Yuen Street. Sha Tin District chief inspector Ng Yuk-pui said that the cameras were seized along with three memory cards found in three separate individual changing rooms at the gym. The gym has two female toilets, one male toilet, and four unisex individual changing rooms, each with a shower area and changing space, Ng said. Police identified the suspect after conducting digital forensic analysis of footage stored on the cards. Ng said the police were not able to reveal how many videos were stored on the cards as the case had entered legal proceedings. Officers also seized hard drives and other devices from Fung's residence. Asked whether the police would take action against sellers of the pinhole cameras, Ng said that the suspect bought the cameras on a well-known mainland Chinese e-commerce platform, which would pose limitations on enforcement. According to local media reports, Fung was believed to have bought the cameras from Taobao.

articles.title: Man, 34, arrested over alleged voyeurism after pinhole cameras found at Sha Tin 24/Fitness branch
articles.description: 27th September 2026 - (Hong Kong) Police arrested a 34‑year‑old local man surnamed Fung in Sha Tin this evening on suspicion of voyeurism following the discovery of suspected pinhole cameras at the 24/7 Fitness branch on Lek Yuen Street. Officers said three changing rooms at the premises were found to contain similar devices. The suspect is being held for further enquiries, with the investigation handled by Sha Tin District Crime Squad Team Two. The case surfaced after a male member reported noticing a tiny blue light within a gap in the suspended ceiling of a single‑occupancy communal shower. Staff removed an object believed to be a covert camera and alerted police at about 5.11pm on 25th September. Responding officers subsequently found two more similar devices at the scene. It is understood the wiring was connected to the ceiling lighting circuit. Checks of other nearby branches under the same operator did not reveal further devices. 24/7 Fitness said it takes the matter seriously and apologised for the alarm caused to members, stressing it has zero tolerance for any intrusion of privacy. The company suspended the affected shower immediately, carried out a full inspection of all showers and changing rooms at the branch in the presence of police, and only reopened facilities after confirming no irregularities. The operator also conducted same‑day spot checks across all branches, focusing on concealed locations such as false ceilings and light troughs, and reported no abnormalities. It reiterated that CCTV is installed only in public areas for security and never in showers, changing rooms or toilets. The firm said staff notified police at the first opportunity and the branch manager has provided a statement. Additional measures include reviewing and strengthening daily cleaning and patrol routines, with increased inspection frequency. The company said it would share further updates in due course without prejudicing the ongoing investigation.

pendingReview.title: Bourbon maker accused of secretly filming guests having sex, including at Kentucky Castle
pendingReview.description: The complaint says footage included sex at Kentucky Castle and other homes. Kentucky bourbon maker Wes Henderson has been accused by family members of secretly filming them, as well as others in multiple places, including at the Kentucky Castle, according to a lawsuit filed in Kentucky. Henderson is a Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame member best known as the founder of Angel's Envy, which was sold for a reported $150 million to Bacardi in 2015. Representatives of Angel's Envy had no immediate response to a request for comment. Later, Henderson purchased The Kentucky Castle in Versailles in Woodford County, a wedding and tourist destination with a hotel and restaurant, and launched a new whiskey brand, True Story, with plans to build a $92 million distillery nearby. Those plans are on hold. What the lawsuit against Wes Henderson alleges In a lawsuit filed in June in Oldham County, family members accuse Henderson of invasion of privacy, voyeurism, and possession or viewing of matter portraying a sexual performance by a minor. The family members did not respond to requests for comment; the Herald-Leader is not naming them due to the nature of the allegations. The lawsuit has been sealed. The lawyers who filed it have not responded to repeated requests for comment about the filing, and neither has Wes Henderson or an attorney who has represented him in other lawsuits. According to the filing, the family members were vacationing in Henderson's home near Melbourne, Florida, in June 2025 when they discovered multiple hidden cameras, including some capable of live-streaming. They subsequently turned over the cameras and recorded footage to law enforcement, according to the lawsuit. Because the case file has been sealed, any response that has been filed by Henderson was not immediately available. No criminal charges have been filed, apparently. Cameras with Wi-Fi, recording devices found According to the filing, the family members removed approximately 15 hidden cameras and their SD cards and returned home, where they reviewed some of the footage, which captured intimate acts as well as images of themselves in various stages of undress and using the restroom. "The cameras also captured the defendant, Wes Henderson, having sex with other women (not his wife). Upon information and belief, the cameras captured other adults having sex, as well as footage of what appeared to be a homeless individual, potentially a minor, who happened to be carrying a portable medical device, using the restroom," according to the filing. In a footnote, the filing noted, "Some of the videos were from SD cards that captured sex at the Kentucky Castle which is connected to a business interest of the Defendant Wes Henderson." Henderson has owned the Kentucky Castle since 2023. He is facing multiple lawsuits for debts related to his distilling and hospitality businesses. The cameras in the Florida home were disguised as fire alarms, behind a mirror, in a fan, in a clock, in a speaker, in a bathroom air vent directly above the toilet, in charging blocks and plug outlet extenders, according to the filing. According to the filing, "there are a total of 40 people identified as being captured without their knowledge." Some of the footage included Henderson placing the cameras and deliberately placing them to capture views of a bed, according to the filing. More cameras found In the filing, the family members allege they notified other relatives and Henderson's wife, who "gave (them) permission to sweep their Oldham County, Kentucky home for similar hidden recording devices." Allegedly, another 15 similar cameras were found there. The filing also alleges that footage "showed Wes placing cameras in various third parties' homes." According to the filing, the family members contacted local authorities and turned over the cameras and SD cards from the Oldham County home and the Florida vacation home. "At present, law enforcement continues to maintain possession of the evidence," according to the filing. It is unclear which law enforcement agency has the cameras and footage. Versailles Police Chief Rob Young said he was not aware of the filing. Oldham County Police Chief Greg Smith also said his department is not involved in the case. "After being confronted, and throughout the last 11 months, Wes Henderson has frequently apologized for his actions and requested forgiveness through several text messages to multiple members of his family," according to the filing. The lawsuit seeks punitive damages for pain and suffering, medical expenses, and a jury trial. Unrelated lawsuits were filed earlier this year in Jefferson Circuit Court against TKC Distilling and related companies that produce True Story. Architects Luckett & Farley, which designed the now-shelved distillery, alleged they are owed more than $936,000. And Bourbon Hall of Famer Peggy Noe Stevens alleges her consulting company is owed more than $510,000 for work done. A third lawsuit, filed in June by GMR Marketing, alleges TKC Distilling owes them more than $120,000. All of those lawsuits are still pending. This story was originally published October 2, 2026 at 11:04 AM with the headline "Bourbon maker accused of secretly filming guests having sex, including at Kentucky Castle."

pendingReview.description: A University of Miami student has been arrested after police said he placed a hidden camera in his roommate's bedroom nightstand and secretly recorded him. South Miami police arrested 21-year-old Dylan Hugh Long on Tuesday on charges of video voyeurism and burglary of an unoccupied structure, according to WSVN. Newly released body camera footage shows officers placing Long in handcuffs on campus. According to the arrest report, the roommate found the hidden camera after noticing a blue light coming from the nightstand and confronted Long, who denied it. After leaving for class, the roommate plugged the camera in and found 49 recordings, several of them corrupted. Some showed Long testing the device, while others captured the roommate walking "to and from the shower without his knowledge or consent," the report states. Long has entered a written plea of not guilty, and his attorney says he maintains his innocence. However, detectives said Long admitted putting the hidden camera in the bedroom, but only to check whether his roommate was reading his text messages without answering them. The roommate did not want to comment when a news crew visited the home. Long told detectives this started over unanswered text messages In body camera video released Thursday, Long tells a detective, "The arguments have been going on for a year with his lack of communication on things I needed to know." South Miami Police Detective Jackie Del Sol said Long "planted the device inside to see if he was receiving his text messages because he had been ignoring him." Long also denied ever viewing the recordings. "I never saw any of the footage. I didn't even know how to see the footage," he told investigators in the interrogation room. He also said the friends in the apartment were "all in each other's rooms all the time," so the idea that nobody should enter a room "was not really a thing." The roommate told police he did not know about the hidden camera and had not given anyone permission to place a recording device in his bedroom. He found the camera on Sept. 12, and body camera footage from that day shows him showing detectives the recordings in his apartment. South Miami police located Long in Coral Gables on Tuesday morning, more than two weeks later. Officers took him to the station for questioning, and he was later transported to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center. As the judge found probable cause in bond court, Long was ordered to stay away from his roommate. Privacy complaints involving hidden watchers have drawn attention elsewhere, including a women's soccer locker room case in which a player reportedly spotted a man above the ceiling. In that case, the man allegedly told police he was reading the Bible. Long's case, by contrast, involves a roommate and a camera hidden in a nightstand. His attorney, Matt Shafran, described the dispute in court as "an argument that happened between roommates and then turned a little different." The defense also told the court that Long has no prior arrest history and has a government job lined up. Bond was set at $3,500, and Long has since bonded out of jail. "Mr. Long maintains his innocence and looks forward to addressing these allegations through the appropriate legal process," Shafran said in a statement. "What occurred was not voyeuristic in nature, and we believe this situation has been significantly misunderstood." Online records list Long as a senior studying political science and economics at the university. The police account and the defense account describe the same events very differently. Police said the recordings captured the roommate without his consent. However, Long's attorney said the situation grew out of an argument between roommates. The hidden camera case remains pending, and Long has not been convicted of any crime. Long is expected to keep contesting the charges as the case moves through court, and further filings or footage could clarify what happened between the two roommates.
